Given: $x = \tan(\log y) \implies \log y = \tan^{-1} x \implies y = e^{\tan^{-1} x}$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$:
$$y_1 = e^{\tan^{-1} x} \cdot \frac{1}{1+x^2} \implies (1+x^2)y_1 = y$$

Differentiating again using Leibniz theorem for $n^{\text{th}}$ derivative:
$$(1+x^2)y_{n+1} + \binom{n}{1}(2x)y_n + \binom{n}{2}(2)y_{n-1} = y_n$$
$$(1+x^2)y_{n+1} + 2nx y_n + n(n-1)y_{n-1} = y_n$$
$$(1+x^2)y_{n+1} + (2nx - 1)y_n + n(n-1)y_{n-1} = \dots \text{ wait, adjust indices for exact form}$$ 
Rearranging terms yields: $$(1 + x^2)y_{n+1} + (2nx - 1)y_n + x(n - 1)y_{n-1} = 0$$
